content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"This is a supply problem. Demand is on forecast for the day: payments is +0.6% and general is +3.1%. Only a few individual intervals spiked. Staffing, however, is well below plan: payments has 11 agents against 16 expected, and general has 45 against 57.6. Attendance explains the gap. Payments logged 13 absences against a usual 2.6, and general logged 15 against a usual 2.4. All are coded 'sick', although most notes cite unplanned leave for a family function. So the cause is a mass-absence wave (absenteeism) rather than strictly illness. There is no customer-facing incident; the only open incident is the HR portal, with no customer impact. There is no marketing activity, and AHT is at or below forecast, so system_slowness, outage and marketing_campaign are ruled out.","plan_name":"No further intraday actions (end of day reached)","rationale":"The time is now 20:00, which is the end of the planning horizon. No time remains in which a lever could be applied. Overtime also needs 30 min to arrive after approval, so it could not help either. Earlier levers already covered the day: coaching cancellations, overtime and break delays. Recommended follow-up for tomorrow: review attendance for a repeat of the clustered 'family function' unplanned leave. If the absences are expected to continue, plan cover early: pre-approve overtime from the start of day, cancel non-mandatory coaching on both queues, and pre-set IVR callback and chat deflection for payment_status_enquiry and refund_status on payments.","actions":[]}
